_comment: Up NEPA! dialogue for the Prologue and Act 1. ALL Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa lines are PENDING NATIVE-SPEAKER REVIEW (Story Bible §10). Every person, brand and agency is fictional. Choice: {text, flag?, value?, fx?, reply?: [lines]}.

p1_intro.text: Ojota! Owambe guests! Lekki! Enter with your change!
Driver, I hope this bus has AC. This lace cost me ₦85,000.
Madam, the AC is the window. Wind is free. Baba God dey!
Adeleke, that your aso-ebi is not original. The colour is shouting "Balogun Market".
At least I didn't sew mine last night with candle light.
Ladies, ladies. We will settle it at the jollof.
Everybody hold body. Royal Pavilion, Lekki. We go reach before the couple enter. I promise you.

p1_chinchin.text: Driver, stop small. I want to buy chin-chin for the road.
Mama, the road is the bridge. It is six minutes.
Six minutes is long. My sugar is low.
Which kind sugar? You've been eating my puff-puff since Ojota.
Nobody is stopping. We are on a mission. The mission is jollof.

reply.text: This driver has no home training.
Ah. God bless you, my son. You will marry a good woman.
I'm already married to this bus.

p1_warden.text: Officer Gbenga. My brother. My guy. My personal nightmare.
Your side mirror is facing the wrong spiritual direction. That one is an offence.

p1_warden_pass.text: VIP? Owambe VIP? …Is it the Adeleke wedding? My cousin's wife's sister is catering!
Go, go! Tell them Gbenga said they should keep me moin-moin.
Sule, if you talk two more words this year, I will promote you.

p1_arrive.text: We have arrived in style! In a danfo, but in style!
Driver, come inside. I know the family. Come and chop.
I'm working. I must find passengers for the return…
Nonsense. Free jollof is not something you reject. Sule, you too, come.
…Baba God dey. Sule, lock the bus.

p2_intro.text: Girls! Listen. Elders first. Then the bride's family. Then everybody else.
Anybody who comes with their own takeaway pack, you call me. I will handle them personally.
And nobody, I repeat NOBODY, comes back for a second plate before the couple's family eats. This jollof is politics.

p2_cousin.text: Aunty, I'm the groom's cousin. From abroad. Just flew in. Please add extra chicken, the flight was long.
From… from London. Near London. Around London side.
Ikorodu. I'm from Ikorodu. I came by BRT. Please, one plate, I'm begging.
Join the queue like a citizen. And greet your mother for me.

choices.text: Give him a small plate anyway

reply.text: Aunty, God will bless you. I will tell everybody in London.

p2_debtor.text: Aunty Boss! The food is excellent, as usual. God bless your hands.
Mr. Okafor. You owe me ₦8,000. Since the last owambe. February.
Ah, Aunty, I sent it! Transfer. It must be the network.
It must be. Write it down. I don't forget.

choices.text: "Pay me before the cake is cut."

reply.text: Before the cake. Yes ma. Definitely. Is the cake… far?

p3_intro.text: Wassup wassup, it's your boy KC Vibes, live from the owambe of the YEAR!
Today we are catching three viral moments. Three! The MC, the money spraying and the gele competition.

p3_mc.text: Ladies and gentlemen! Put your hands together for the groom's mother, who will now dance for the THIRD time!
Content! Pure content! The MC is a national treasure.
Where are my money sprayers? Make it rain! Make it pour! Make it flood!

p3_trip.text: And the gele competition is… oh no. Oh NO. The bride's mother!
She tripped on her own gele. On camera. In 4K.
I'm deleting it. I am deleting it right now. Respect for elders.

reply.text: KC deletes it. (He did not delete it.)

p4_mc.text: And now, the moment! The couple's first dance! DJ, give me something for the soul!
Light for All! Terms and conditions apply! Ha ha!
Chief, please, keep your voice down. The bag… the bag is under the table.
Ledger, relax. Who will steal from me in my own mother's friend's daughter's wedding?

p4_light.text: Everybody freeze! Nobody move! …Why is everybody frozen in a dancing pose?
MY BAG! Where is my bag?! LEDGER!
It was here! It was just here! It must be… the opposition! Yes. The opposition did it.
Bro. I recorded EVERYTHING. In the dark. With flash.
Sule. We are going home. Now.
Somebody owes me for forty plates of jollof that disappeared in the dark. I'm writing it down.

m11_intro.text: Sule, today we make money. No owambe, no wahala, no Chief, no bag stories.
Oshodi to Obalende, then back over the bridge. Full bus both ways. Baba God dey!

m11_fares.text: Driver, I gave you ₦1,000 since Oshodi. Where's my change?
Dey come from where? From heaven?
Madam, in this life, change is a journey. Not a destination.

m11_goslow.text: Driver, this go-slow is spiritual. I can see my house from here, and my house is in Ikeja.
Everybody calm down. I know these roads like I know my own pocket. Empty, but I know them.
Wait. I can see it. The gap. The holy gap.

m11_nextime.text: Driver, I no get change. I'll pay you next time.
Next time? Oga, there is no next time in danfo! This is not a subscription!
Next time. God's time is the best.
Sule, two words in one day? What's happening to you?

m11_bag.text: Sule. Sule, come and see. Close the door.
That is the Chief's bag. From the owambe. The one everybody is looking for.
Nobody saw anything. Nobody knows anything. We are not in this.

reply.text: Don't.

m12_intro.text: Aunty Boss! Ajo day! The women are ready. Some of them are ready to argue.
Mama Nkem, ajo is trust. Trust is money. And money, I don't forget.
Six women. Six contributions. Nobody leaves the market until I say so.

m12_w1.text: Aunty, here is my ₦5,000. Complete. Count it twice.
I counted it three times while you were bringing it out. Thank you, my sister.

m12_w2.text: Aunty, I'll pay double next week. My tomato spoiled.
Your tomato spoiled last week too. Tomato does not spoil every week.

reply.text: …Here. ₦5,000. Please stop looking at me like that.
Half today, half in my prayers. Thank you, Aunty.

m12_w3.text: Aunty, have you heard? They say the Chief's bag grew legs and walked away.
Gossip is free. Ajo is ₦5,000. Bring it.

m12_w4.text: Aunty, I've transferred it! Look, here's the screenshot.
This screenshot is from 2023. The date is right there. And it's in the old naira design.

choices.text: "You owe me ₦5,000. And now ₦500 for insulting my eyes."

m12_w5.text: My own is ready. And I brought you agbalumo.
This is why you will collect first next month.

m12_w6.text: Last one. Mine. Plus the market council dues.
Mama Nkem, you're the only person in Lagos who has never owed me.
Because I have seen what you do to debtors, my sister.

m12_pos.text: Aunty, the POS queue is long today. And Konnekt network is… you know.
"Network don fail, come back tomorrow." I know. Let me handle it.
When the network fails, tap SWITCH NETWORK or HOLD IT AT THE WINDOW before the customer's patience runs out.

m12_dispute.text: Aunty! This woman says I owe her ₦200 for pepper!
It was ₦200 for pepper AND she touched my tomatoes with her eyes!
Both of you. Silence. The ₦200 dispute will be settled. Today.

choices.text: Split it: ₦100 each, and everybody shakes hands

reply.text: Wisdom. Pure wisdom. Solomon is shaking.

choices.text: Pay the ₦200 yourself to end the noise

reply.text: Aunty Boss is paying? Write it in the newspaper!

choices.text: The Stare. On both of them.

reply.text: …We are no longer quarrelling. We are friends. Since childhood.

m12_whisper.text: Aunty… come closer. Two men came here this morning. One in a red shirt, one big like a fridge.
They were asking for "a canteen woman in the video". The video from the owambe. The one where the light went.
The one with forty thousand views, Aunty. You're in it. Covering a pot.
Write it down. KC Vibes. I don't forget.

m13_intro.text: Guys. GUYS. The blackout clip. Forty thousand viewers. FORTY THOUSAND.
who took the bag (eyes)  ·  zoom on the table!!  ·  is that a canteen aunty lol
I'm going live right now to break it down frame by frame. Phone battery is at…
…4%. And NEPA has taken light. Again.
Okay. Okay okay okay. Content creators don't panic. We adapt. Somebody in Yaba has power.

m13_barber.text: My generator, my rules. ₦200 to charge. And you must give me your opinion on this haircut.
That is… a bold fade. Very bold. Brave, even.
Thank you! Nobody appreciates art in this area. Plug in.

m13_church.text: You can charge. The church has an inverter. But you must sit until the end of the prayer.
Pastor started at 9. It's 11. We are on point 3 of 12.
lollol bro is trapped  ·  AMEN  ·  type 1 for blessings

m13_kiosk.text: Charge Am Here! Thirty phones, one socket, zero wahala.
It's not smoking. It's thinking. ₦100, plug in.

m13_reveal.text: Okay chat, frame 412. Look at the hand going under the table. That's the bag. And that face is…
That face is the CHIEF'S OWN TREASURER. The man is—
??? continue!!!  ·  KC??  ·  it froze  ·  he don japa lol
Guys… guys? The signal. The signal dropped exactly there. Of course it did.

m13_pepper.text: Hey! You! Purple shirt! You're the boy in the video!
Me? No. I'm his twin. He's in Abuja. Like and subscribe!
Come here! The Chief wants to "discuss content" with you!

m13_canteen.text: Aunty, please, there's a man chasing me, I just need five minutes—
You are KC Vibes. You filmed me covering my pot in the dark. Forty thousand people have seen my elbow.
You owe me an explanation. And ₦2,500 for the malt you're about to drink. Sit. Food is ready.

m14_intro.text: Two men came to the park. Red shirt. Big man. They asked for a yellow danfo.
Sule, every danfo in Lagos is yellow.
With "Baba God Dey" on the back.
…Okay. We need to hide the bus. Alhaji Mechanic in Mushin. He owes me.

m14_passenger.text: Driver, I am going to Mushin. I have paid. Full journey.
Madam, today is not a good day. Please come down.
I have paid for the full journey. I am not coming down. I will be filing my nails.
Pepper and Salt are coming. Keep them away. Passengers will shout directions: vote on the turns. The heat meter shows how close they are.

m14_hide.text: Alhaji! Cover the bus! Now now now!
Tunde, you still owe me for the last gearbox.
Your account is a book. A full book.
This is my stop. Thank you, driver. Five stars. Very exciting service.
We need help. Somebody with sense.
I know one woman in Surulere. Her canteen has a generator and she fears nobody.

m15_open.text: So. A danfo driver, a content creator, and a bag of money. In my canteen. At night.
Madam, I just need somewhere to keep it for one night. One night!
Aunty, the whole internet is looking for this bag. I can make it a series—
Nobody is filming anything inside my canteen. Generator! Somebody add fuel!

m15_standoff.text: The bag was under seat 4! I didn't steal anything!
I have the video! It was the treasurer! Ledger!
Lower your voices, my customers are sleeping upstairs!
If the Chief finds this bag with us, we're finished!
If the internet finds it with us, we're FAMOUS!
If either of you breaks my plate, you're both finished AND famous!
We should hide it somewhere nobody will look!
We should give it back with a camera running!
We should count it! Nobody makes decisions about money they haven't counted!

m15_bag.text: Wait. Bring that bag here. Look at this handle.
This stitching. Double cross, then a knot. This is MY stitching. I sewed this bag. Three years ago. For a client.
A man who paid with "transfer, I've sent it". I never forgot his face.
Tunde, you've gone quiet. Tunde doesn't go quiet.
I'm just tired. Long day. What do we do with it?

m15_return.text: The next morning, at the Chief's campaign office…
You want to return a bag? To the Chief? Which bag?
The Chief has not lost any bag. The Chief has never had a bag. Who sent you?
Go away before we arrest you for… for… bringing a bag.
So they can't admit it's theirs. Interesting. Write it down.

m15_count.text: Nobody decides anything about money that hasn't been counted. Tunde, the rubber bands. KC, put down that phone and count.

m15_diary.text: Wait. What's this? Stuck between the notes… a page.
"Paid: Rally ₦4.5m. Paid: 'consultants' ₦12m. Paid: Light for All transformer… ₦0."
It's a diary. Somebody wrote down everything.
Somebody who doesn't forget. I like this person already.

m15_hide.text: Under the rice. Nobody looks under fifty kilos of rice.
Thieves who want my rice will meet my Stare.

m15_close.text: Listen, both of you. From today, we talk every day. Nobody does anything alone.
No group chat. Group chats are where peace goes to die.

m21_intro.text: Sixty kVA. Second-hand. Alhaji says it has "character".
It has character. It also has one wheel that likes to go left. Respect it.
Aunty, why are we moving it at night?
Because in the daytime, every street in Mushin will want it. Generators are politics.
And at night, every street in Mushin is awake because there's no light. Same wahala.

m21_rivals.text: STOP THERE! Is that a generator I see on MY street?
Oga Slippers. Good evening. It's… a big radio.
A radio with an exhaust pipe? Boys! Bring the slippers!
Tunde, step aside. Let me speak to him.

m21_stare.text: Ma. Good evening, ma. I didn't see you there, ma. Please, pass. Pass with joy.
Forty years of collecting debts. Move.

m21_light.text: Light? LIGHT? From a generator in Surulere? Boys, drop the slippers! Bring the speaker!
They're… dancing. The rival street is dancing to our generator.
Everybody is family when there is light. KC, you can charge your phone here now. Ask me first.

m22_intro.text: Okay. Nobody knows I'm here. Not Tunde. Not Aunty. Just me and my documents.
Northvale has scholarships for content creators. Real ones. I could learn. Come back. Maybe.
Should I tell Aunty first? She'll find out anyway. She finds out everything.

reply.text: Thank you for telling me. Go and do your interview. And KC — answer like you have sense.

m22_pass.text: APPROVED. They approved me. The officer still didn't blink, but they APPROVED me.
…Now I have to decide if I'm actually going. Why is that harder?

m22_fail.text: Refused. "Insufficient ties to grandmother's goat." I don't even HAVE a grandmother's goat.
It's fine. It's fine. Content. This is content. …It's not fine.

m22_caught.text: KC. What is this receipt? "Republic of Northvale. Visa application fee."
Aunty, I was going to tell you—
Aunty, please say something. The silence is worse.

m22_confessed.text: The officer asked about a goat.
They always ask about the goat. Sit down. Food is ready.

m23_intro.text: Red car. White car. Pepper. Salt.
Driver! I am a prophetess. The Lord has shown me a turn of favour. When I say turn, you TURN.
Madam, the Lord and I will discuss it at the junction.

m23_convoy.text: Wedding convoy! Sule, horn! Wave! Look happy!
Where did the yellow bus go? There are… there are twelve yellow buses with ribbons!
Pepper, I'm hungry. Is there jollof at this wedding?
Driver, five stars. The prophetess was wrong about every single turn, but five stars.

m24_intro.text: Mama Chief's 90th. Every big person in Ikoyi will be there. And Barrister Ledger's study is in that house.
How do we get in? We're not invited.
In Lagos, nobody is invited. People just arrive in the correct aso-ebi.

m24_aunties.text: Ah! My daughter! You look familiar. Whose child are you?
I'm… the caterer's sister. From the bride's side. Of the family. Of the event.

choices.text: Change the subject: "Your gele is magnificent!"

reply.text: You noticed! It took four people and a ladder.
…Okay. Okay. Enjoy the party, my dear.

m24_aunties.text: I am married to my business, ma.
Hmm. A business cannot carry you to the hospital.
A business can BUY the hospital, ma.

m24_mama.text: You. The woman with the eyes. Come here.
Happy birthday, Mama. Ninety years. God has been faithful.
Ninety years, and I have never seen anybody look at my son's guards like you just did. I like you.
My son is a fool. A loud fool. If you have come to cause trouble… cause it well.

m24_study.text: Barrister Ledger's study. Files. Files. A photo of Ledger shaking hands with… himself? In a mirror.
And here. Under the drawer. Two pages. Same handwriting as the page in the bag.
"Paid to Light & Darkness 'consultant': ₦7m. Transformer delivered: none."
KC is still dancing. I should leave before they make him do the shoki.

m25_intro.text: Ledger didn't take the Chief's money to a bank. Banks ask questions. He took it to POS agents. Forty of them.
Small small, so nobody would notice. But POS agents talk, Aunty. We all talk.
We are not copying him. We are FOLLOWING him. Every receipt is a witness.

m25_tosin.text: The sweating man? Nine withdrawals. Always ₦490,000. Never ₦500,000. As if ₦10,000 makes him invisible.

m25_kunle.text: Every Tuesday. Briefcase. He tipped me ₦200 and asked me to "forget his face". His face is unforgettable, Aunty.

m25_bisi.text: Aunty Boss! I have been waiting for somebody to ask me. I kept a receipt for EVERY transaction. My mother taught me.
Mrs. Bisi, you are a national treasure.
Rubber bands, by month. Highlighter, by amount. Do you want them by colour also?

m25_done.text: Forty agents. Eighteen million. All roads lead to Barrister Ledger, and Ledger leads to the Chief.
If you need me to say it on camera, I'll say it. With receipts.
Write it down. We don't forget.

m26_intro.text: The only open PetroNaija in three districts. The queue starts in Mushin and ends in my dreams.
We need diesel for the canteen generator. Or KC's phone dies, and then he cries.
The pump is literally running. I can hear it.

m26_stare.text: …There is a little fuel. For you, ma. Only for you, ma.
HEY! That convoy is skipping the queue! Who do they think they are?!
Oh no. Somebody has thrown the first jerrycan.

m26_done.text: Two jerrycans of diesel. One small bump on the head. A victory.
Back of the queue. Where democracy lives.

m27_intro.text: We have receipts. We have diary pages. We have Mrs. Bisi. Now the ward needs to KNOW.
Only the truth, KC. If you post one lie, they will use it to bury everything else.
Only gists with receipts. I promise. …Mostly promise. Okay, fully promise.

m27_radio.text: Brethren! This so-called "diary" is the work of the enemy! Call now and get the anointed Light for All ringtone, only ₦2,000!
He's selling ringtones to defend the Chief. On air. Live.

m27_done.text: the RECEIPTS lol  ·  Ledger is sweating through the screen  ·  Teacher 2027!!
Ward-wide. Danfo, market, WhatsApp, church women, students. Everybody is talking.
Good. Now let's see who is talking back.

m28_open.text: Tonight we count all of it. Everything. Nobody sleeps until we know what's in this bag.
Can I at least film the counting?
You can film your own funeral if you touch my rubber bands.

m28_twist.text: Wait. This note. Hold it to the light.
It's… old. These are the old notes. They were withdrawn ages ago. Nobody takes these anymore.
Mostly. The Chief has been hoarding paper. Sitting on it like a hen on a stone.
I did the maths on my fleet money. I'm going to lie on the floor now.
Wait. The handle. My stitch. Double cross, then a knot… I always sew a hidden pocket behind that knot.
…Three more pages. The diary. THIS is what Ledger was really carrying.

m28_confess.text: …I have to tell you people something.
Four years ago, I drove the Chief's campaign bus. Rallies. Paid crowds. Promises I knew were lies. I needed the money for Baba God Dey.
That's why I went quiet when Aunty saw the stitching. I knew that bag. I carried bags like it.

choices.text: Aunty: "We all have a past. What matters is today."

reply.text: You owe me ₦3,500 for pepper soup. That is the only debt between us. Get up from the floor.

choices.text: KC: "You should have told us from the start."

reply.text: You're right. I'm telling you now. That has to count for something.

m28_choice.text: So. The old notes. They're worthless to us, but they're proof the Chief was hoarding.
Or… I know a guy who says he can still "change" old notes. For a fee.
What do we do with them?

choices.text: Hand them over (to the WIEC and the press, with the receipts)

reply.text: Correct answer. We are not becoming the Chief.

choices.text: Keep them. KC's guy might come through

reply.text: This is a mistake. Write it down: I said so.
It's just a backup plan, Aunty.

m31_intro.text: Good morning, Tunde. I am told you have a bus, and I have a megaphone. Between us, that is a campaign.
Mrs. Okon! You taught me to read. You also flogged me in Primary 4.
And look at you now. Reading road signs. Drive. Six blocs, one week. We win them with the truth.
At each stop, win the bloc over. Evidence and honest promises move votes. Bribes always backfire.

m31_traders.text: The market women want to know: what will Teacher do about the light?
Market traders, what is your pitch?

choices.text: Show Mrs. Bisi's receipts: the transformer money that vanished

reply.text: Receipts! Women, did you hear? RECEIPTS.

choices.text: Promise a market generator in 100 days

reply.text: Hmm. Promises are free. We'll see.
An ENVELOPE? To ME? Women! Teacher's driver is bribing us! (She posts it in four WhatsApp groups.)

m31_drivers.text: Drivers want to know about the agberos.

choices.text: Read the diary page: the Chief paid agberos to harass you

reply.text: …The whole park is quiet. That means they're angry. At him.
They took the vouchers. They're voting for the Chief. He gave bigger vouchers.

m31_students.text: Students want data, light to read, and a reason to stay in Lagos.

choices.text: Teacher's plan: a ward reading room with solar light

reply.text: A reading room? With LIGHT? Sign me up.
The data expired in an hour. Like the promise.

m31_church.text: The church women want peace, and they want the truth told with respect.
Church women, what do we offer?

choices.text: A town hall in the church compound, open to all

reply.text: A town hall. In the open. That is respect.

choices.text: Aunty Boss caters the town hall (free food)
Donate to the building fund, loudly

reply.text: The Lord sees donations. So did the Pastor's camera. It's on Miracle FM now.

m31_okada.text: The okada union chairman says the Chief promised them a new park. Four years ago.
Okada riders, what is our pitch?

choices.text: Show the diary: the park money went to "consultants"

reply.text: Consultants?! The chairman just threw his helmet.

choices.text: Promise safety training and a registered park
Pay the chairman to endorse Teacher

reply.text: He took the money. And endorsed the Chief. He's a businessman.

m31_youth.text: Oga Slippers representing the youth! We want jobs, light and a football pitch.

reply.text: She scored an own goal and laughed about it. She's one of us.

choices.text: Promise the stadium lights stay on after the rally
Pay them to wear Teacher T-shirts

reply.text: We wore them. Inside out. To the Chief's rally. With his T-shirt on top.

m31_poll.text: That's the week. Win or lose, we told the truth in every street.
WIEC poll is on the phone, Mrs. Okon. It's… close.
Then the debate and the rally will decide it. Get some sleep, Tunde. And sit up straight.

m32_intro.text: Gidi Gist FM is hosting the ward debate. The Chief said he'd skip it. Unless…
Unless his mother tells him to go. I called Mama Chief.
My mother says I must attend. I am attending. Light for All! Terms and conditions apply!
Good evening, ward. Let's talk about the terms. And the conditions.

m32_done.text: This debate was rigged! By… by reality!
Thank you, everyone. Go home safely. Use a torch.
Chat is on fire. Twelve thousand watching. Teacher is trending.

m33_intro.text: For the rally plan to work, the light has to come back at EXACTLY the right second. Only one man can do that.
Light Man himself. He doesn't take bribes. He's "a professional".

m33_bayo.text: You want me to restore power to the stadium at a specific second? That's against procedure.
I don't take money. I'm a professional.
…But my shift ends soon, and I haven't eaten. Mallam Garba's suya. In Victoria Island. Extra yaji. HOT.

m33_suya.text: Mallam! Your best suya. Extra yaji. It's for a professional.
The suya is hot. The clock is running. Go!

m33_deal.text: …Still hot. Extra yaji. Onions on the side.
Tomorrow night. When the Chief takes the stage, I take the lever. You'll have your light.

m34_intro.text: My people! Light for All! Terms and conditions—
The light goes off. As planned.

m34_reveal.text: Good evening, Agbado-Ketu. My name is Ngozi Eze. You know me as Aunty Boss. I'm going to read you some receipts.
Transformer for the ward: paid zero naira. Consultants: twelve million. Rally crowd: four and a half million. Jollof for the Lekki owambe: never paid. To the kobo.
And this is the diary of Barrister Ledger, live to every phone in this stadium. Page by page.
I… I just wrote things down! That's what a treasurer does! I'm sorry, Chief!
Ledger! You wrote DOWN the bribes?!
Olusegun. Come down from that stage. Now.

m34_win.text: The people have spoken. And for once, they've been heard. Thank you.

m34_lose.text: We lost by a few hundred votes. But the Chief is under investigation, and the whole ward knows the truth.
That is not nothing. That is the start of everything.
We go again. Write it down.

m35_airport.text: My flight to Northvale leaves in two hours. The scholarship is real. The cold is also real, apparently.
Whatever you decide, decide it with your full chest.
Baba God Dey will drive you either way. Back home, or to the gate.

reply.text: I'll come back with skills. And a jacket for Aunty. And I'll call every day.
Every day. I'll be counting.
There's too much content here. And too much family.
Then get in the bus. We have passengers.

m35_a.text: Ladies and gentlemen: the Agbado-Ketu Central transformer. And the borehole. Paid for, delivered, and with receipts.
Tunde, I'm forgiving your debt. In public. ₦3,500. Everyone heard it.
Baba God Dey is the ward shuttle now. Free on Sundays. Sule, say something.

m35_a_full.text: Honest ending, complete: you tried to do right from the start, the old notes went to the right people, and the three of you trust each other.
Family Meeting, best group chat in Lagos.

m35_b.text: Three weeks later. A knock at the canteen door. FCIB.
"The guy" was an FCIB informant. Of course he was.
I said so. I wrote it down. Page one.
Three people eating separately. The generator hums. Nobody talks.

m35_c.text: Hello? Can you see me? It's minus four here. MINUS. I didn't know numbers went that way.
Aunty, "Aunty Boss Kitchen TV" has 200,000 subscribers in Northvale. They want your jollof recipe.
Tell them Baba God dey. Even in the snow.

m35_d.text: The last page. Behind the stitch. Ledger wrote one more name. Above the Chief's.
Who's that? I've never heard of…
I have. I drove for him once. A long time ago.
Then this isn't over. Family Meeting. Tomorrow. Bring the bus.
